notes.zh: 我们活着，就像做梦——独自一人……

reference.context: 马洛讲述经历时，承认自己很难传达当时完整的生命感受。随后他又说，听众也可能从他身上看见当时的自己看不见的东西。这里呈现的是叙述与理解之间的距离。
reference.question: 有没有一种经历，我以为已经讲清楚，对方却仍没有机会真正接近它？

notes.zh: 淑女和卖花女的区别，不在她的举止，而在别人如何对待她。
notes.en: the difference between a lady and a flower girl is not how she behaves, but how she’s treated.

notes.zh:
伊萨卡给了你这趟奇妙的旅程。
没有她，你就不会启程。
如今，她已没有什么可以再给你。
notes.en:
Ithaka gave you the marvelous journey.
Without her you would not have set out.
She has nothing left to give you now.
notes.source: C. P. Cavafy · Ithaka · Keeley–Sherrard revised translation, 1992

reference.author: C. P. Cavafy
reference.date: 1992 revised translation copyright; first translation copyright 1975
reference.locator: Three sentences beginning “Ithaka gave you”; C. P. Cavafy: Collected Poems, Revised Edition, edited by George Savidis, Princeton University Press.
reference.sourceType: 诗人官方档案 Onassis Cavafy Archive 刊载的出版英译。
reference.chineseStatus: 本次据 Keeley–Sherrard 修订英译转译，非既有出版中译；未核对希腊语原文。

reference.originalText:
Ithaka gave you the marvelous journey.
Without her you would not have set out.
She has nothing left to give you now.
reference.context: 诗把归返伊萨卡的旅程写成充满见闻、感官与学习的一生。目的地给人的礼物，是让人出发并在路上成长，而不一定是在抵达后再兑现某种财富。
reference.question: 当一个目标没有给我预想中的奖赏时，我能否看见它已经带来的经历和成长？
reference.verification: 2026-11-03：实际打开 Onassis 官方档案的 Ithaka 全文及版本署名，核对所引三句；此版本是 would not，未套用另一转载本的 wouldn’t。页脚明确 Collected Poems Revised Edition、Keeley、Sherrard、Savidis 及版权 1975、1992。日期指所用英译版权版本，不冒称原诗写作年。

notes.zh:
寻找一个能孕育未来的此刻，
让未来像面包一样
滋养我们的孩子。
notes.en:
seeking a now that can breed
futures
like bread in our children’s mouths
notes.source: Audre Lorde · A Litany for Survival · 2020 institutional excerpt

reference.author: Audre Lorde
reference.locator: Opening stanza, the three consecutive lines beginning “seeking a now”; NYS Writers Institute, University at Albany, archival post.
reference.sourceType: 纽约州作家学院、University at Albany 文学档案刊载的原诗节录。
reference.chineseStatus: 本次据所核英文诗行翻译；以滋养传达面包意象，非既有出版中译。
reference.englishStatus: 英语原诗连续三行节录，保留小写起句及原行序，未添加原句没有的结尾标点。
reference.originalText:
seeking a now that can breed
futures
like bread in our children’s mouths
reference.context: 诗人写处在不断抉择的边缘、承受不安的人，也写他们为孩子寻找未来。面包这个日常意象，使未来成为切实的生存与滋养。
reference.question: 我想为下一代留下的未来，是否也落实为今天能让他们安稳生活的东西？
reference.verification: 2026-11-03：实际阅读 NYS Writers Institute 刊出的开篇诗节，核对从 seeking a now 到 children’s mouths 的连续三行及署名 Audre Lorde。记录学院页面发布与更新日期，明确它们是机构节录本日期，不把 2020 写成诗的创作年。

notes.zh: 希望是美好的，也许是最美好的事物，而美好的事物永不消逝。
notes.en: Hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies.
notes.source: Andy Dufresne · The Shawshank Redemption · 1994 film, screenplay

reference.author: Andy Dufresne (Frank Darabont, screenwriter)
reference.locator: Printed page 123, PDF page 124 of 126; Andy’s letter to Red, read in voice-over after Red retrieves the envelope beneath the rock.

reference.originalText: Hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies.
reference.context: 离开监狱后的瑞德找到安迪留下的信。安迪邀请他继续向前，仍为他留着位置。这句话出现在两人曾经争论希望是否危险之后。
reference.question: 我是否因为害怕再次失望，就把仍然可能的生活也拒之门外？

notes.zh: 但那又怎样呢——答案必定在尝试本身。
notes.en: But who cares - the answer must be in the attempt.

reference.author: Celine (Richard Linklater & Kim Krizan, screenwriters)
reference.locator: Printed page 63, PDF page 64 of 73; Celine’s reflection on the space between people and the difficulty of truly understanding another person.

reference.originalText: But who cares - the answer must be in the attempt.
reference.context: 塞琳说，人与人之间也许存在某种魔力，来自试着理解对方、分享一些东西；即使完全理解几乎不可能，尝试本身仍有意义。这里的那又怎样，回应的是无法完美理解的限制。
reference.question: 我是否因为无法完全理解一个人，就不再认真尝试靠近他？

notes.zh: 没有希望的批判性思考，是犬儒；没有批判性思考的希望，则是天真。
notes.en: Critical thinking without hope is cynicism. But hope without critical thinking is naïveté.
notes.source: Maria Popova · Cartographer of Meaning in a Digital Age · 2015

reference.author: Maria Popova
reference.work: Cartographer of Meaning in a Digital Age, On Being

reference.originalText: Critical thinking without hope is cynicism. But hope without critical thinking is naïveté.

reference.question: 我的怀疑是在帮助我更准确地行动，还是在替我放弃行动找理由？

notes.zh: 有许多事情，你无法为之感恩。但在每一个时刻，你仍然可以心怀感恩。
notes.en: There are many things for which you cannot be grateful. But in every moment, you can be grateful.

reference.author: David Steindl-Rast
reference.work: How to Be Grateful in Every Moment, On Being
reference.locator: Conversation with Krista Tippett at Gut Aich Priory, St. Gilgen, Austria; answer distinguishing gratitude in a moment from gratitude for violence or suffering.
reference.sourceType: On Being 原始英语访谈，2020 年机构重播转录。
reference.chineseStatus: 本次据所核英文摘录翻译，非既有出版中译。

reference.originalText: There are many things for which you cannot be grateful. But in every moment, you can be grateful.
reference.context: 他明确说，人无法为战争、暴力和疾病感恩；但当下仍可能有学习、成长，甚至站出来抗议的机会。他区分对遭遇的认可与对仍可回应的机会的珍惜。
reference.question: 面对不愿接受的事情，我还能珍惜或争取哪一种回应它的机会？

notes.zh: 人的一切活动，都由欲求推动。
notes.en: All human activity is prompted by desire.
notes.source: Bertrand Russell · What Desires Are Politically Important?, Nobel Lecture · 1950-12-11

reference.author: Bertrand Russell
reference.work: What Desires Are Politically Important?, Nobel Lecture
reference.locator: Opening argument after the introductory discussion of politics and psychology; followed by Russell’s explanation of the desire to be dutiful.
reference.sourceType: 诺贝尔奖官方网站发布的英语演讲全文。

reference.originalText: All human activity is prompted by desire.
reference.context: 罗素在这篇演讲中把愿意履行道德义务，也视为一种欲求。他希望人们不只看物质处境，也看各种动机及其相对强弱，而不是把欲求简单等同于贪婪。
reference.question: 当我说自己只是在尽义务时，背后还藏着哪些愿望与期待？

notes.zh: 我们知道，那套历法并不通用于全世界；但时间是共通的，时代的迫切要求也是如此。
notes.en: That calendar, we know, is not universal, but time is, and so are the imperatives of time.
notes.source: Wole Soyinka · This Past Must Address Its Present, Nobel Lecture · 1986-12-08

reference.author: Wole Soyinka
reference.work: This Past Must Address Its Present, Nobel Lecture
